title: NVIDIA Control Panel Not Opening or Missing? 7 Fixes in Order
description: NVIDIA Control Panel often fails to open because a service stopped or the Store app is missing. Restart NVIDIA Display Container LS first; 6 more fixes here.
dek: Why the NVIDIA Control Panel will not launch, disappears from menus or opens to missing pages, and the fixes in the order to try them.
quickAnswer: Start with the service: press Windows + R, type services.msc, find NVIDIA Display Container LS, set it to Automatic and click Start. If the Control Panel is missing entirely, install it from the Microsoft Store. If neither works, do a clean reinstall of the NVIDIA driver. On laptops, a message about no NVIDIA display usually means your screen is wired to the integrated graphics.
intro: This page is for GeForce owners on Windows 10 or 11 whose NVIDIA Control Panel will not open, opens and closes, is missing from the Start menu or right-click menu, or shows only some of its pages. Causes are listed from most to least common, each with its fix, followed by the NVIDIA App as an alternative and the rare signs of a hardware fault.

steps.h: Close any stuck copy and try again
body: Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager. If NVIDIA Control Panel is listed under Apps or Background processes, select it and click End task, then open the Control Panel again from the Start menu. A copy that hung on a previous launch can block new ones without showing a window.

A full restart, not shut down and power on with fast startup enabled, reloads the display driver and its services. Choose Restart from the Start menu power options. This alone fixes a Control Panel that stopped opening after the PC woke from sleep.

steps.h: Open it from the Start menu
body: Search the Start menu for NVIDIA Control Panel rather than relying on the desktop right-click menu. On Windows 11 the entry is hidden under Show more options when you right-click the desktop, so it can look missing when it is not.
If those quick steps do not help, find the section below that matches what you see. They are ordered from the most common cause to the least, so starting at the top saves time.

sections.h: Clicking NVIDIA Control Panel does nothing, or it opens and closes
body: The most common cause is a stopped NVIDIA service. The Control Panel depends on a Windows service called NVIDIA Display Container LS. If that service is stopped or set to Disabled, often by a tuning or debloat tool, the Control Panel either fails silently or flashes open and closes.

To fix it, press Windows + R, type services.msc and press Enter. Scroll to NVIDIA Display Container LS and double-click it. Set Startup type to Automatic, click Apply, then click Start if the service status is Stopped. If it was already running, right-click it and choose Restart. Then open the Control Panel again.
If the service will not start, or stops again after a restart, the driver installation is likely damaged; skip to the clean reinstall section.

sections.h: NVIDIA Control Panel is missing entirely after a driver install
body: Current NVIDIA drivers for Windows are DCH drivers, a Microsoft driver format in which the NVIDIA Control Panel is a separate Microsoft Store app rather than part of the driver itself. NVIDIA's full installer from nvidia.com normally adds it. Drivers installed by Windows Update, or by a laptop or PC maker's image, often expect the Microsoft Store to add it afterward, and if the Store is disabled, blocked by a work policy or slow to sync, the Control Panel never appears.

Open the Microsoft Store, search for NVIDIA Control Panel and install the app published by NVIDIA Corp. It is free. If the Store is not available on your PC, install the current driver package from nvidia.com instead, which is the route NVIDIA supports for most desktop users. Avoid copies of the Control Panel from third-party download sites.

sections.h: It stopped working after a driver or Windows update
body: A driver that Windows Update installed over NVIDIA's, or an update that did not finish, can leave the Control Panel app and the driver at mismatched versions. The Control Panel may then refuse to open or show an error that NVIDIA display settings are unavailable even on a desktop.

The fix is a clean reinstall. Download the current driver, run the installer, choose Custom installation and tick the clean installation box. If that does not help, remove the driver with DDU in Safe Mode while offline, then install the fresh package. Both procedures are covered step by step in [how to update NVIDIA drivers](/how-to-update-nvidia-drivers/).

sections.h: Laptop says you are not using a display attached to an NVIDIA GPU
body: This message is expected on many laptops. The built-in screen is wired to the Intel or AMD integrated graphics, and the GeForce GPU renders games and passes frames through it. Because the NVIDIA GPU does not drive the screen directly, the Control Panel either shows this message or hides display pages such as resolution and color settings.

If your laptop has a MUX switch, setting it to use only the discrete GPU, in the laptop maker's control software or the BIOS, connects the screen to the NVIDIA GPU and unlocks those pages. Many gaming laptops also wire one external port, often HDMI or a USB-C port with DisplayPort output, directly to the NVIDIA GPU; plugging a monitor into that port does the same for that display. The 3D settings pages remain available either way, and display settings for the built-in screen can still be changed in Windows Settings or the integrated graphics control software.

sections.h: NVIDIA Control Panel is missing from the right-click menu
body: On Windows 11, the desktop right-click menu shows a shortened list. Click Show more options, or click an empty spot on the desktop and press Shift + F10, to see the full menu, where NVIDIA Control Panel appears when installed.

If it is missing from the full menu too, open the Control Panel from the Start menu, open its Desktop menu at the top and make sure Add Desktop Context Menu is ticked. If the Start menu has no entry either, the app is not installed, so follow the missing Control Panel steps above.

sections.h: It opens but crashes, freezes or shows blank pages
body: A Control Panel that launches but crashes on a particular page, hangs while loading or shows empty panels usually has a damaged settings store or app install. Because it is a Microsoft Store app, Windows can repair it.

Open Settings, go to Apps, then Installed apps, find NVIDIA Control Panel, open its menu and choose Advanced options. Click Repair first, which keeps your settings. If that does not help, click Reset, which clears the app's data and restores defaults, then reopen it. If the problem persists, do the clean driver reinstall described above.
One more case: the Control Panel does not work in a Remote Desktop session, since Windows swaps in a remote display driver. Change NVIDIA settings at the PC itself.

sections.h: Can you use the NVIDIA App instead of the Control Panel?
body: For most settings, yes. The NVIDIA App's Graphics section has global and per-program 3D settings, such as low latency mode, power management mode and frame rate limits, and its System section covers display settings including G-SYNC and resolution on supported setups. NVIDIA has been moving Control Panel features into the app since it launched, though a few advanced options remain Control Panel only.

If the Control Panel is broken and you need to change a setting today, the NVIDIA App is a practical workaround. It also handles driver updates and the in-game overlay; if you would rather not have the overlay, see [how to turn off NVIDIA Overlay](/how-to-turn-off-nvidia-overlay/).

sections.h: When to RMA or replace the graphics card
body: A Control Panel that will not open is almost always a software issue. Suspect the hardware only if, after a clean driver reinstall, Device Manager shows the GeForce card with a Code 43 error, the card disappears from Device Manager entirely, the NVIDIA installer reports that it cannot find compatible graphics hardware on a desktop card, or you see artifacts and corruption before Windows loads.

Before filing a warranty claim, shut down, switch off the power supply and unplug the PC, then touch bare metal on the case to discharge static. Reseat the card, push each power connector fully home and try another display cable and output. If you can, test the card in another PC. If it fails there too, contact the seller or card maker. If you need a replacement, see the [best graphics card](/best-graphics-card/) guide.

mistakes: Disabling NVIDIA services to save resources

Debloat scripts and tuning guides sometimes disable every NVIDIA service. NVIDIA Display Container LS is needed for the Control Panel, and stopping it breaks the app without any meaningful performance gain. Leave it set to Automatic.
Downloading the Control Panel from random sites

Some sites offer the NVIDIA Control Panel as a standalone download. Get it only from the Microsoft Store, published by NVIDIA Corp., or through NVIDIA's own driver installer. Repackaged copies can be outdated, mismatched with your driver or bundled with unwanted software.

A missing or crashing Control Panel rarely needs a Windows reinstall. The service restart, Microsoft Store install, app repair and clean driver reinstall fix almost every case, in far less time and without losing your apps.

The message about not using a display attached to an NVIDIA GPU is normal on most laptops with hybrid graphics. The GeForce GPU still runs your games. Check the laptop's MUX or display mode setting before reinstalling drivers.
bottomLine: When the NVIDIA Control Panel will not open, restart the NVIDIA Display Container LS service first, since a stopped service is the most common cause. If the app is missing entirely, install it from the Microsoft Store or reinstall the full driver from nvidia.com. Updates that leave mismatched versions need a clean reinstall, and a crashing app can be repaired from Windows Settings. On laptops, missing display pages are usually expected. The NVIDIA App covers most of the same settings in the meantime.

faqs.q: Why is NVIDIA Control Panel not opening?
faqs.a: The most common reason is that the NVIDIA Display Container LS service is stopped or disabled. Restart it in services.msc and set it to Automatic. Other causes are the Control Panel app missing after a Windows Update driver install, a driver version mismatch after an update, or a damaged app that needs repair.

faqs.q: How do I get NVIDIA Control Panel back?
faqs.a: Install it from the Microsoft Store by searching for NVIDIA Control Panel, published by NVIDIA Corp., or reinstall the full driver from nvidia.com, which normally includes it. On Windows 11, also check under Show more options in the desktop right-click menu, where it is hidden by default.

faqs.q: Is NVIDIA Control Panel being replaced by the NVIDIA App?
faqs.a: NVIDIA has been moving Control Panel settings into the NVIDIA App since the app launched in 2024, and the app now covers most 3D and display settings. The Control Panel is still available and still holds some options, so both exist side by side for now.

faqs.q: Why does NVIDIA Control Panel only show 3D settings?
faqs.a: On most laptops, the built-in screen is connected to the integrated graphics, so NVIDIA's display pages are hidden. The 3D settings still control how games run on the GeForce GPU. Switching a MUX to discrete GPU mode, or using an external port wired to the NVIDIA GPU, unlocks the display pages.

faqs.q: Does NVIDIA Control Panel work over Remote Desktop?
faqs.a: No. During a Remote Desktop session, Windows uses a remote display driver, so the NVIDIA Control Panel cannot reach the GeForce GPU and will not open properly. Make changes while sitting at the PC, or use other remote access software that keeps the physical display driver active.

faqs.q: Can I download NVIDIA Control Panel without the Microsoft Store?
faqs.a: The supported way without the Store is to install the full driver package from nvidia.com, which normally adds the Control Panel. Avoid standalone copies from third-party sites; they may not match your driver version and can carry unwanted software.

faqs.q: Will reinstalling the NVIDIA driver delete my settings?
faqs.a: A normal install keeps them. A clean installation or a DDU removal resets NVIDIA settings, including per-program 3D profiles and custom color settings, to default. Note any settings you rely on before a clean reinstall so you can set them again afterward.
